newsitem.title: USA: La. evacuates workers after fumes near barge.
newsitem.headline: La. evacuates workers after fumes near barge.

text.p: Thousands of Louisiana state workers were being evacuated after gases near a petrochemical spill on the Mississippi made some feel ill, a spokesperson for the governor said Wednesday.

"We're not sure that it is benzene but there is a strange smell that is making some employees suffer from dizzinesss and blurry vision," said Angele Davis, deputy commissioner for communications at Louisiana governor Murphy Foster's office.

"We've talked with state police and are mandating that downtown state employees located along the river be evacuated. It does not affect the state capital, that decision is being left up to governor, the speaker of the house and the president of the state senate," Davis said.
The incident occured at approximately 1030 EST and there are approximately "a couple of thousand" workers affected by the evacuation, Davis added.
The Department of Environmental Quality and the state police were looking into the cause, she said.
She said it wasn't clear if the apparent gas leak was related to a grounded barge near Baton Rouge which was leaking benzene and toulene, toxic petrochemicals.
The barge broke loose and was beached last week when the surging Mississippi made navigation more difficult.
